case_title: Chotkau v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_socioeconomic_status: Very poor; could not afford a lawyer in the Sessions Court and an amicus was provided
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (niece, as stated in the prosecution complaint). No prior enmity between accused and victim found by the court.
evidence_type: Circumstantial (last seen theory) based on testimony of PWs 1 to 3; post-mortem; recovery of clothing. No medical examination of accused; forensic report not produced.
aggravating_circumstances: Victim a six-year-old girl; rape and murder (as held by the Sessions Court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302 and 376; sentenced to death
high_court_outcome: Conviction and death sentence confirmed on reference and appeal
neutral_facts: The accused was charged with raping and murdering a six-year-old girl, who was a relative of the accused. According to the complaint lodged by the victim's uncle, at about 4:00 p.m. on 8 March 2012, during the Holi festival, the accused took the victim away on the pretext of showing dance and song performances. When the victim did not return home, a search was made. The accused was not found at home, and the victim's body was found in a sugarcane field on the southern side of the village. A member of the search party stated that he saw the accused leaving the sugarcane field about half an hour later. Another villager said he saw the accused carrying the victim towards the sugarcane field. The prosecution case rested on these eyewitness accounts and on the last-seen circumstance. The FIR was registered at the police station on the evening of 8 March 2012. The post-mortem was conducted by a doctor, who prepared a vaginal smear. A salwar bearing stains was sent for forensic examination, but no forensic report was obtained. The accused was not subjected to medical examination. The investigating officer recorded witness statements and prepared a site map. The victim's clothing, including a salwar, was recovered by the police.
physical_harm: Death of the six-year-old victim; rape alleged. Nature of injuries not described in detail.
key_evidence_accepted: None of the eyewitness evidence of PWs 1 to 3 was accepted as reliable. The Court relied on the absence of medical examination of the accused as fatal to the prosecution.
witness_credibility: PWs 1 to 3 found completely untrustworthy due to serious contradictions on FIR lodging, the place and handling of the body, inquest details and clothing. Lower courts had wrongly treated these as minor.
post_offence_conduct: Alleged: absconding after the body was found (relied on by lower courts). Not established as reliable by the Supreme Court.
trial_duration: offence: 08.03.2012; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 18.04.2016; Supreme Court: 28.09.2022
legal_representation: Appellant: S. Nagamuthu, Sr. Adv., with others. State: Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad, AAG, with others.
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed and final report submitted; trial held. Forensic report not obtained; accused not medically examined.
procedural_irregularity: FIR received by the CJM five days late with no explanation; no one identified as taking the FIR to court; contradictory FIR and inquest evidence; no medical examination of accused; forensic report not obtained.
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced to death. High Court: confirmed on reference and appeal. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, conviction and sentence set aside.
prosecution_argument: No reason for PWs 1 to 3 to implicate the accused; their evidence was found cogent by two courts; the FIR delay did not prejudice the accused; s.313 defects do not vitiate findings absent prejudice; forensic evidence is not always mandatory.
defence_argument: PWs 1 to 3 untrustworthy; unexplained five-day FIR delay; serious contradictions on the body and inquest; last seen evidence insufficient; key witnesses not examined; forensic/medical evidence not produced; s.313 not complied with.
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain excluding innocence (panchsheel); FIR delay assessed under s.157(1) CrPC for creditworthiness; medical evidence under s.53A CrPC is important where the victim is dead and the case rests on circumstantial evidence.
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda (1984) 4 SCC 116; Meharaj Singh (1994) 5 SCC 188; Bhajan Singh (2011) 7 SCC 421; Brahm Swaroop (2011) 6 SCC 288; Balram Singh (2003) 11 SCC 286; State of Rajasthan v. Daud Khan (2016) 2 SCC 607; Jafarudheen (2022 SCC OnLine SC 495); Krishan Kumar Malik (2011) 7 SCC 130; Rajendra Pralhadrao Wasnik (2019) 12 SCC 460
other_sentence_order: Release forthwith unless wanted in connection with any other case
